questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I visited Amsterdam before my exchange and I really liked the city and I could imagine myself living there. Additionally, I have heard a lot of good things about Dutch universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a long and a bit complicated process to figure everything out before my exchange but it was really worth in the end. When I had any questions about the exchange I emailed either my home or host university and they always tried to help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
My university in Amsterdam had organized two days of practical introduction days where you could find many answers to questions about e.g. registration, insurance, language courses. 
Vrije Universiteit has a big and quite organized exchange programme, which is very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was very lucky to know somebody with a spare room in Amsterdam, so I was not dependent on student housing. A few friends also found housing by themselves (which is really difficult but not impossible) and we lived 5 minutes apart from each other in the West, which was super nice. 
Most people I got to know did live in the campus housing, which also sounded very fun. And even though I didn't live there, I could always come and join the parties and other activities that were happening in the student housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be very difficult to find a room in Amsterdam if you don't know anybody there but you can be lucky to find something via Facebook, instagram or other sites.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: My host uni sent me emails about all the steps I had to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always email the exchange office at the VU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I chose to register for a minor, which the host university suggested. I chose the minor Social and Organizational Psychology because I wanted to take some classes that were similar to A&O at KU, which I would have followed back home in the 5th semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: By choosing a minor you won't have any subjects or exams that overlap and you will also see some of the same people in the different classes which can be quite nice and familiar.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had a lot of multiple choice exams and I think the educational level at KU is a bit higher. 
I enjoyed that the courses, assignments and exam preparations did not take up so much.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It has a similar structure - I had both lectures and classes for most of the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Evolutionary psychology
M&D: Individual and Organizational Diagnosis
Professional Skills
Human Resource Management
Group Dynamics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the course Professional Skills because it was so different from the courses that I have had at KU. It was very intimate and helpful because it was more practical (e.g. working on your networking and presentation skills) and entailed a lot of self-reflection.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarket items are less expensive but going out for dinner or drinks is quite similar to DK. I can recommend to bike a lot as public transport is quite expensive over time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any clubs or sports activities as I lived quite far from uni.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can register for the gym and sports classes at uni.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The university in Amsterdam has a great focus on sustainability. They have some great events and activities that revolve around that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I stayed a lot in Amsterdam over the weekends because there was so much to explore and so many great events I wanted to attend. 
It is also nice to go on a small trip to the beach which is really close or to Belgium.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust because the Dutch culture is quite similar to the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you get a job in the city or do some group work with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Biking in Amsterdam is more chaotic than in Copenhagen but you get used to it pretty quickly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think in general that the Dutch culture is very lively and laid back, which is nice to experience. Additionally, Amsterdam is very international which creates a great diverse atmosphere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to explore many different areas in Amsterdam, as they all have something different to offer. 
Having a bike in Amsterdam is really helpful.
It is nice to have some money saved up for your semester abroad so you can enjoy it fully and don't have to worry about money.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Getting a Revolut bank account makes it easier to transfer money internationally.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to know so many great people from all around the world and Amsterdam is just such a great city to live in. I would really recommend doing your exchange in Amsterdam!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't think there were any great challenges during my exchange. The registration process before your exchange can be difficult but it is worth it in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
